about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pumpkin and Sweet Potato Congee
recipes.summary: Silky rice porridge simmered with pumpkin and sweet potato, topped with spring onion and sesame.
steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in the water with the ginger and salt for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains burst and the porridge is thick.
Add the pumpkin and sweet potato and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until completely tender and starting to fall apart.
Stir well, loosen with hot water if needed and top with soy, sesame oil, spring onion and sesame seeds.
notes: Stir often near the end so the base does not catch.
Congee thickens as it cools; add water when reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Spring Onion Congee
recipes.summary: Savoury rice porridge with browned mushrooms, ginger and a drizzle of sesame oil.
steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in the water with the ginger and salt for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy and thick.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil in a hot pan for 6 minutes until golden, add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant and splash in the soy.
Stir the mushrooms into the congee, then serve topped with spring onion, sesame oil and white pepper.
notes: Cook the mushrooms in batches so they brown rather than steam.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Chilled Carrot and Ginger Soup
recipes.summary: A smooth, bright carrot soup with fresh ginger and orange, served cold with yoghurt.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the ginger and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrots and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Blend until completely smooth, stir in the orange juice and salt, then chill for at least 3 hours.
Serve topped with yoghurt and chives.
notes: Thin with cold water if the soup thickens as it chills.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Chilled Buttermilk and Herb Soup
recipes.summary: A cooling no-cook soup of buttermilk, cucumber and fresh herbs.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, then cool in cold water and peel.
Whisk the buttermilk, yoghurt, cucumber, garlic, herbs, lemon juice, salt and pepper together.
Chill for 1 hour until cold, then ladle into bowls and top with radish and egg.
notes: Taste before serving and add salt if needed as chilling dulls flavour.
Food safety: boil eggs until firm and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within 2 days.

recipes.title: Beef Pho Broth with Rice Noodles
recipes.summary: Aromatic star anise and ginger beef broth poured over rice noodles and thin sliced beef.
steps: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes until blackened in spots.
Simmer the stock with the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, fish sauce and sugar for 30 minutes until deeply fragrant, then strain.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, drain and divide among bowls.
Top with the raw beef, ladle over the boiling broth until the beef changes colour and is cooked through, then add sprouts, herbs, lime and chilli.
notes: The broth must be bubbling hot when it hits the beef.
Food safety: thin beef must be cooked in the boiling broth to at least 63°C (no pink remains); keep leftover broth refrigerated and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Clear Chicken Broth with Vegetables
recipes.summary: A simple, clear chicken soup with shredded chicken, carrot, celery and thyme.
steps: Place the chicken, water, onion, bay leaf, thyme and salt in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer, skimming off any foam until the surface is clear.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and is cooked through, then lift out, shred and discard the onion, bay leaf and thyme.
Add the carrots and celery to the broth and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken, add the pepper and parsley and serve hot.
notes: Keep the broth at a gentle bubble so it stays clear.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Mushroom Ginger Broth with Rice Noodles and Greens
recipes.summary: A light, savoury mushroom and ginger broth with soft tofu, noodles and bok choy.
steps: Simmer the stock with the mushrooms, ginger, soy and vinegar for 10 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until soft, then drain and divide between bowls.
Add the bok choy and tofu to the broth and cook for 2 minutes until the bok choy is tender and the tofu is hot.
Ladle over the noodles and finish with spring onion and sesame oil.
notes: Add the tofu gently so it stays in cubes.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the noodles.

recipes.title: Silverbeet and Chickpea Soup with Lemon
recipes.summary: A wholesome chickpea soup with silverbeet and lemon, with a little garlic and cumin.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the chickpeas are soft, mashing a few against the pot.
Stir in the silverbeet and cook for 4 minutes until wilted and tender, then add the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
notes: Mash some chickpeas to thicken the soup naturally.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.title: Cream of Celery Soup with Thyme
recipes.summary: A smooth, gently flavoured celery soup with potato, thyme and a swirl of cream.
steps: Cook the onion and celery in the butter for 10 minutes until soft without colour.
Add the potato, stock and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is falling apart.
Remove the thyme, blend until smooth, then stir in the cream, salt and pepper and heat gently until hot.
notes: Strain the soup for a very smooth finish.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Leek and Pearl Barley Broth
recipes.summary: A rustic broth of leek, carrot and pearl barley with parsley.
steps: Soften the leeks, carrots and celery in the oil for 8 minutes until the leek is soft.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the barley is plump and tender.
Remove the bay leaves, season and stir in the parsley.
notes: The barley absorbs liquid, so add water when reheating.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Hearty Minestrone with Cannellini Beans
recipes.summary: A thick vegetable minestrone with beans, small pasta and basil.
steps: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the zucchini, cannellini beans, green beans and pasta.
Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the pasta is tender, then season and finish with basil.
notes: Add extra stock if the pasta soaks up too much liquid.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Chilled Beetroot Soup with Yoghurt and Dill
recipes.summary: A vivid pink chilled beetroot soup with yoghurt, cucumber and dill.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beetroot and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the beetroot is very tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the vinegar, sugar and salt and chill for 3 hours.
Whisk in half the yoghurt, ladle into bowls and top with cucumber, dill and the remaining yoghurt.
notes: Wear gloves or an apron as beetroot stains.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Laksa with Rice Noodles and Tofu
recipes.summary: A creamy coconut laksa with sweet pumpkin, tofu puffs and rice noodles.
steps: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant, then add the pumpkin, stock and coconut milk.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the pumpkin is tender, then add the tofu and heat for 3 minutes until hot.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, drain and divide into bowls.
Season the soup with lime juice and soy, ladle over the noodles and top with sprouts and coriander.
notes: Use less paste for a milder soup.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the noodles.

recipes.title: Zucchini Lemon Orzo Soup
recipes.summary: A light, lemony orzo soup with zucchini and dill.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and zucchini for 3 minutes until lightly coloured.
Add the stock and bring to the boil, stir in the orzo and simmer for 9 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the lemon juice, zest, dill and salt and serve topped with feta.
notes: Orzo keeps absorbing liquid, so thin leftovers with stock.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Japanese Takikomi Gohan Mixed Vegetable Rice
recipes.summary: Rice cooked with mushrooms, carrot and edamame in a light soy broth.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then place in a pot with the water, soy, vinegar and ginger.
Scatter the mushrooms and carrot over the top without stirring, cover, bring to the boil and cook on low for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the edamame, cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes until the rice is tender, then fold through the sesame oil and seeds.
notes: Do not stir while cooking so the rice steams evenly.
Food safety: cool leftover rice within 1 hour and refrigerate; use within 1 day.

recipes.title: Israeli Couscous with Roast Vegetables and Lemon
recipes.summary: Pearl couscous tossed with roast zucchini, capsicum and red onion in a lemon herb dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C, toss the vegetables with 1 tbsp oil and roast for 25 minutes until tender and charred at the edges.
Cook the couscous in the boiling water for 8 minutes until tender, drain any excess and cool slightly.
Toss with the roast vegetables, remaining oil, lemon juice, salt, parsley and toasted pine nuts until evenly coated.
notes: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Eat warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Lebanese Batata Harra Spiced Potatoes
recipes.summary: Crispy cubed potatoes tossed with garlic, chilli and coriander.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, drain well and let the steam rise.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the potatoes for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Add the garlic, chilli, ground coriander and salt for 1 minute until fragrant, then toss with fresh coriander and lemon juice.
notes: Let the potatoes steam-dry before frying for extra crispness.
Eat the same day.

recipes.title: Quinoa Breakfast Bowl with Poached Egg and Spinach
recipes.summary: Warm quinoa with wilted spinach, a poached egg and a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer in the water for 15 minutes until tender and the germ has spiralled out, then drain well.
Wilt the spinach in the oil for 1 minute until soft and stir through the quinoa with the salt and lemon.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes until the whites are set, then drain.
Top the bowls with avocado, eggs and chilli flakes.
notes: Rinse quinoa well to remove any bitterness.

Food safety: poach eggs until the whites are fully set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

recipes.title: Egg White Omelette with Mushrooms and Herbs
recipes.summary: A light, high-protein omelette with mushrooms, spinach and herbs.
steps: Fry the mushrooms in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, add the spinach for 30 seconds until wilted, then tip out.
Whisk the egg whites with the salt, pepper and herbs, pour into the same pan and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes until nearly set.
Spoon the mushrooms over half, fold and cook for 1 minute until the egg is fully set.
notes: Use a non-stick pan so the whites slide out easily.
Food safety: cook until the egg is firm throughout.

recipes.title: Autumn Apple and Celery Salad with Walnuts
recipes.summary: A crisp, juicy salad of apple, celery and walnuts in a light mustard dressing.
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, honey and salt together.
Toss the apple and celery with the dressing right away until every slice is coated, so the apple stays pale.
Fold in the walnuts, parsley and rocket and serve immediately.
notes: Slice the apple just before assembling.
Best eaten the same day.

recipes.title: Charred Cabbage Wedges with Miso Butter
recipes.summary: Cabbage wedges roasted until charred and tender, glazed with garlicky miso butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C, brush the cabbage with the oil and roast cut side down for 20 to 25 minutes until charred at the edges and tender in the centre.
Mash the butter with the miso, garlic and honey.
Dot the hot wedges with the miso butter until it melts, then scatter with sesame and spring onion.
notes: Do not move the wedges while roasting so they char.
Miso butter keeps 1 week in the fridge.

recipes.title: Braised Leeks with Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.summary: Tender braised leeks dressed warm in a sharp mustard vinaigrette with parsley.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool, peel and chop.
Simmer the leeks in the stock, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes until completely tender, then drain well.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, honey and salt, pour over the warm leeks and top with parsley and egg.
notes: Wash the leeks thoroughly between the layers.
Food safety: boil eggs until firm and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Cucumber Pickle Salad
recipes.summary: Crunchy cucumber with sweet and sour rice vinegar, chilli and herbs.
steps: Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber and carrot with the dressing and chilli and leave for 10 minutes to lightly pickle.
Top with mint and peanuts and serve cold.
notes: Salting the cucumber first makes it crunchier.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
